result.summary: Surgical fix for the CN's per-query parked-output bookkeeping (report finding B4, plan issue 2). One idea, three files, all in experimental/starrocks/src: the engine thread tags every ParkedOutput with its query_id, keeps a bounded failed-query memory, drops only the failed query's parked outputs on Err (the process-wide wipe survives only for unlabelled fixtures), skips any later Run of a failed query before touching the GPU, and exposes one fire-and-forget request AbandonQuery. Two CN call sites invoke it: run_ready_fragment's Err arm (covers the q16 translation-failure leak and every other pre-run failure) and cancel_plan_fragment gated to reasons other than QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH (the FE cancels every instance of every query, reason 5 or 1 on success, measured 642 cancels in cn1/cluster.log, so the gate is what keeps the 15 passing queries untouched). local_exchange.rs, result_store.rs, nixl_transport.rs, engine C++ and FE are untouched. result.mechanism: engine.rs: (a) ParkedOutput gains query_id: Option<FragmentInstanceId> copied from request.label.query_id at park time (engine.rs:710-716). (b) A FailedQueries map (id -> first cause, FIFO-capped at 1024) lives on the engine thread next to parked/parked_slots/poisoned (engine.rs:267-275). (c) In the Run arm (engine.rs:282-318) a Run whose label.query_id is in FailedQueries is answered Err("fragment of query .. skipped: the query already failed on this CN: <cause>") before context.fragment()/build()/GPU work. (d) The Err arm's wipe body (engine.rs:301-315) becomes abandon_query(parked, parked_slots, poisoned, failed_queries, request.label.query_id, err): retain parked entries of other queries, poison only the dropped slots (poisoned.clear() first, today's bound), record the failure; query_id None keeps today's process-wide wipe. (e) New EngineRequest::AbandonQuery{query_id,cause} with no respond channel (must never wait behind a running fragment, same rule as the staging bypass at engine.rs:16-21); handler = abandon_query. FIFO on the existing channel: a Run queued before it runs and parks then is dropped, a Run queued after is skipped. fragment_executor.rs: trait method abandon_query(query_id, cause) -> Result<(), String>, default Ok(()) (a stub parks nothing); SiriusEngine sends without receiving. compute_node_service.rs: (f) run_ready_fragment Err arm (:877-897) calls executor.abandon_query(query_id, error) after results.fail_query, covering translation failure (:1361), output-name mismatch (:1347), sink validation (:1066-1131), drain failure (:872); (g) cancel_plan_fragment (:457-479) keeps results.cancel and additionally calls abandon_query when request.query_id is Some and cancel_reason is not QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH (proto internal_service.proto:464-482; FE DefaultCoordinator.java:1028-1034 success reasons, :764-786 failure reasons, :1161-1167 error_message only for INTERNAL_ERROR). Measured cases: q05: 5774's Err records q05 and drops its 2 slots; the worker's later Runs 5773/5777/5776 and receiver 5775 (which today relayed 11 batches and parked 4.69 GB, cluster.log 6072-6305) are skipped; q06's first fragment starts ~0.72 s earlier at allocated=0. q16: senders ff87/ff86 parked 6.6 GB, receiver ff85 failed translation on the worker (cluster.log 16593) -> abandon_query drops both. q21->q22: leftovers acc (179 ms) and acb (3153 ms, 36.64 GB) skipped. Passing queries: one HashMap::get on an empty map per Run, no Err path taken, cancels with reason 5/1 take the unchanged path; no added engine message, no ordering or determinism change. Sync dispatch mode (default off): Runs already queued on the engine channel at failure time still run and park, then the AbandonQuery that follows drops them; the campaign ran with async dispatch (capture-cn.sh:12) where nothing is queued ahead. Explicit non-goals: LocalExchange removal by query (stale PendingReceiver is host-side KBs; a readied receiver of a dead query is skipped anyway), aborting a running fragment (fix 1), ResultStore changes.

risks: R1 Sync dispatch mode (SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH unset, the default): Runs already queued on the engine channel when the failure lands still execute and park; bounded to fragments whose RPCs arrived before the failure (all within ~100 ms), and they are dropped by the AbandonQuery that follows; no regression vs today; the measured config had async on

R2 Replacing the process-wide wipe removes the accidental 'next failure cleans the previous leak' safety net; covered by abandoning explicitly on engine Err, on every worker pre-run Err, and on every FE cancel with a non-success reason; the unlabelled (query_id None) case keeps the wipe

R3 Cancel gate: for QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH nothing of the query is parked by construction (single-batch result model, receiver runs only after all senders parked); every other reason abandons; regression-neutral since today nothing is dropped on any cancel

R4 4-CN: AbandonQuery dropping a slot mid remote drain makes the next export_packed_next return the poisoned cause, the drain fails and the transport's drop_parked warns (nixl_transport.rs:409-418), identical to today's wipe

R5 A skipped result fragment's error reads 'skipped ... already failed: <cause>'; fail_query keeps the first cause per query (result_store.rs:174-179) and the text embeds the original; in sync mode a skipped sender's RPC returns INTERNAL_ERROR to an FE that is already cancelling (DefaultCoordinator.java:1056-1058 'we can't cancel twice')
R6 poisoned map: cleared and refilled on every abandonment that drops something, exactly today's bound
R7 FailedQueries: capped at 1024 with FIFO eviction; unique ids make a false skip impossible; a missed skip needs a fragment pending across 1024 failures (> FE timeout)
R8 Fire-and-forget send fails only when the engine channel is closed (shutdown); logged at warn

R9 Log noise: a skipped fragment still emits 'fragment run started'/'fragment run failed' from run_labeled and an error! in run_ready_fragment; cosmetic, acceptance grep uses the 'skipped' marker; a ResultStore-side check in run_labeled is deliberately left out (second mechanism for the same predicate)

result.summary: Replace the CN's process-wide parked-output wipe with one query-scoped teardown, ServiceCore::terminate_query(query_id, cause), reachable from three triggers (a fragment failure on the engine or CN side, an FE cancel_plan_fragment, a TTL sweep) and acting on four subsystems: a new ParkedRegistry<F> on the engine thread (keyed by query, drops only that query's fragments, tolerates the transport's late drop_parked), two run gates (dispatch worker/run_labeled and engine dequeue+park) that refuse fragments of a dead query, LocalExchange::remove_query/remove_receiver_instance (purges rendezvous state and releases staged remote leases), and the result store (fail_query on INTERNAL_ERROR, release-only on QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH). Idempotent, non-blocking cancel handler, one structured 'query teardown' log line per trigger, two knobs. result.mechanism: Measured today (cn1/cluster.log, headroom.txt): after each of the six failures the engine Err path wipes every parked slot (engine.rs:291-316), then the dead query's queued senders still run on the engine thread (dispatch_worker compute_node_service.rs:380-390 and run_ready_fragment :864-909 have no notion of a dead query) and park 0-36.64 GB nobody consumes (q05 4.69, q08 8.83, q09 31.56, q16 +6.60, q17 4.00, q21 36.64 GB; 0.72/1.04/0.39/6.42/3.35 s of engine time stolen); q16's translation failure never reaches the engine so its 6.6 GB of parked inputs is never dropped; cancel_plan_fragment (:457-482) only marks the result store, and the FE's first cancel arrives 0.25 ms AFTER the next leftover sender started, so Err-time bookkeeping on the CN is mandatory and cancel is the second line. On 1 CN the wipe itself was not the leak (only the failing query's slots were parked); the leftover runs are. Design: (1) engine.rs maps -> ParkedRegistry<F> in parked.rs with ParkedOutput{query_id,...}, torn_down map replacing `poisoned`, drop_query(query)->DropReport, release() returning Ok(AlreadyTornDown) for torn-down slots (transport's post-eos drop_parked stays correct), get_mut() -> Err naming the teardown cause; a shared Arc<Mutex<HashMap<QueryId,cause>>> `terminated` checked at Run dequeue (GATE 1) and again before park (GATE 2, drops output of a fragment whose query died mid-run); Err marks the query on the engine thread itself. (2) FragmentExecutor::terminate_query(query_id, cause) non-blocking: inserts into `terminated`, posts EngineRequest::DropQuery without waiting (never blocks behind a running fragment). (3) ServiceCore.lifecycle map; terminate_query called from run_ready_fragment's Err arm (covers engine failures, translation failures with slots in hand, drain failures), from inline RPC Err in process_fragment, and from cancel_plan_fragment by reason (3/4/2 -> Cancelled + fail_query_all with the FE's message; 5/1 -> Finished, release-only; finst_id (0,0) query-level; missing query_id -> today's behaviour + instance purge). Dispatch gates in run_ready_fragment and run_labeled skip fragments of terminated queries and log 'skipping fragment of a terminated query'. (4) LocalExchange records receiver->query at register_receiver/push_sender; remove_query and remove_receiver_instance return purged SenderSources so staged remote batches' leases are staging_release'd. (5) TTL sweep on the engine thread (SIRIUS_CN_PARKED_TTL_SECS default 1800, warn at half) for an FE that never cancels; retention of terminated/torn_down 600 s. FE facts verified: BackendServiceClient.java:192-209 always sets query_id, error_message only for INTERNAL_ERROR; DefaultCoordinator.java:1003-1035/1161-1177 cancels every deployed instance on failure (INTERNAL_ERROR) and on eos (QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH).

result.summary: Per-query retirement of parked sender outputs in the Sirius StarRocks CN: replace the process-wide wipe in engine.rs with a query-scoped retire, refuse runs of a retired query at both the CN dispatch layer and the engine thread, retire on pre-run failures via the existing fail_query site, and turn cancel_plan_fragment into a real per-query teardown (parked outputs, rendezvous entries, staged leases). One CN PR (two commits), no engine C++ change, no FE patch, no proto change, no new knob. Full design with file:line excerpts at /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/parked-bookkeeping-upstream.md.
result.mechanism:
Principle: the engine holds parked state; the CN decides when a query is over; every retirement is keyed by the query id already carried in FragmentLabel (fragment_executor.rs:57-63, filled at compute_node_service.rs:1584-1589).

(1) New CI-compiled module parked_registry.rs: ParkedRegistry<F> replaces the three loose maps and free functions in engine.rs (parked/parked_slots/poisoned at :267-275, missing_slot :369-377, export_next :380-403, release_slot :408-425, park block :697-717). Each parked entry records query_id; retire(query_id, cause) drops only that query's fragments and poisons only its slots (replace-never-accumulate bound kept). RetiredQueries is a bounded FIFO (const 64) of dead query ids with causes.

(2) engine.rs: the Err arm (:291-316) calls retire(request.label.query_id, err) instead of parked.clear(). run_fragment (:430-481) refuses a run whose query is in RetiredQueries before creating a fragment, inside the function whose Err path already sweeps un-pushed remote-input leases (:462-478). RetiredQueries is an Arc<Mutex<..>> shared with the SiriusEngine handle (same off-thread precedent as the staging arena handle, :129-138) so a cancel can refuse runs already queued in the FIFO request channel. New fire-and-forget EngineRequest::RetireQuery{query_id,cause}; SiriusEngine::retire_query marks the shared set first, then sends. FragmentExecutor gains retire_query(query_id, cause) with a no-op default next to drop_parked (:220-223); drop_parked keeps its exactly-once contract for nixl_transport.rs:790/:412.

result.summary: Progress-gated futility abort for the OOM reschedule loop. The reservation gate (gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:163-296) flags a retried task's attempt as futile only when four independent signals agree: the downgrade sweep that just ran freed 0 bytes, the granted reservation is below the task's OOM-derived retry floor, no task has completed anywhere on the context since this task was rescheduled, and no first-attempt task is in flight on any executor. The reschedule path (:311-419) counts an attempt as futile only if it was flagged AND then OOMed (and the epoch is still unchanged); after max_futile_attempts (default 2, configurable, 0 disables) consecutive futile attempts the query is failed with an error naming usage/limit, resident bytes outside live reservations, grant vs floor, bytes freed and attempts. MAX_RETRIES=100 and the 50 ms backoff stay as the hard cap/pacing (now sirius.executor.pipeline.oom_retry config), so the cross-GPU batch-lock contention case (prepare-path OOM with a full grant and a first attempt running on the other GPU) keeps today's budget. result.summary: Surgical fix for "six queries cannot run on 1 CN": CN-only, TPlan-level fusion of single-destination local leaf senders into their receiver. When a leaf sender (no EXCHANGE_NODE of its own) arrives with a DATA_STREAM_SINK that is HASH_PARTITIONED to exactly one destination on this CN, whose registered receiver expects exactly one sender on that exchange and whose exchange node is plain (no sort_info/limit/conjuncts, row_tuples equal, parent not an AGGREGATION_NODE), the CN does not run it: it stores the sender's TExecPlanFragmentParams as a new SenderSource::LocalFused in LocalExchange. When the receiver's sender set completes, the sender's TPlan.nodes are spliced in place of the EXCHANGE_NODE, its scan ranges merged, the exchange removed from per_exch_num_senders, and the fused plan translated/run as one fragment. All six failing fragments are exactly this shape (measured from the dumps: HASH_PARTITIONED, 1 destination, per_exch :1, leaf FILE_SCAN, no output_exprs). scores.notes: Removes every measured 1-CN leak (4.69/8.83/31.56/+6.60/4.00/36.64 GB, headroom.txt base@start) and the 11.9 s of leftover-fragment time: engine-side Err marks the query on the engine thread before the next dequeue, so in the campaign's async mode (capture-cn.sh:12) 5773/5777/5776/5775 and q21's acb are skipped; the worker Err arm at compute_node_service.rs:877-897 covers q16's translation failure; reason-gated cancel (proto :464-471, generated starrocks.rs:3266-3271) keeps the 15 passing queries on an unchanged path (cancels are reason 5/1 only, cn1-cnlog.txt). Two as-written defects cost points. (1) The engine skip is placed at the Run dequeue (engine.rs:282-318) BEFORE run_fragment, so a skipped Run's remote_inputs never reach the lease sweep at engine.rs:462-478: on 4 CNs a dead query's receiver with staged batches in hand leaks its staging-arena leases for the process lifetime, which is a regression against today (today the leftover receiver runs and the push loop releases them). Fix is a placement change: put the check as the first statement inside run_fragment, exactly where the upstream design puts it. (2) No CN-side gate: in async mode a dead query's sender still goes through execute_ready_fragment -> translate -> run_labeled and emits 'fragment run started'/'fragment run failed' before the engine refuses it (the design's R9/R10), so the plan's literal acceptance line 'no fragment run started for a dead query' does not hold; the design substitutes elapsed_ms<=5 + a 'skipped' marker. The design also understates itself in R1/2.4: after an engine-side Err the engine-local FailedQueries is set before the next dequeue, so queued Runs in sync mode ARE skipped; only CN-side failures and cancels have the FIFO window. Core retain logic lives in cfg-gated engine.rs, so CI never runs it (lib.rs:51-52; experimental.yml:79); only the two GPU tests do. ~110 code + ~240 test lines, three files, one fork PR, half a day.

Covers everything measured plus the multi-CN cancel cleanup (rendezvous purge + staged-lease release), idempotent late drop_parked, TTL sweep, retention, telemetry, three knobs. GATE 1 sits at the Run dequeue and therefore has the same lease-sweep bypass as the surgical skip, mitigated only by the CN-side gate and remove_query's lease release (a cancel racing an in-flight dispatch still leaks). PR 3 (sweep/knobs/docs) is scope beyond the measured problem: the FE already cancels every multi-instance query (DefaultCoordinator.java:1027-1034, measured cancels=N), so the accidental-sweep loss is covered without a timer. Three stacked fork PRs, 3.5-4 engineer-days; the stack's PR 2 alone touches compute_node_service.rs, local_exchange.rs and result_store.rs and is borderline for one sitting. Test plan is the best of the three (CI-tested registry, component tests in both dispatch modes, 4-CN smoke) and its acceptance greps match the plan literally.

Covers the measured leaks and stolen time, q16, the inline-path failure recording, staged-lease release on refusal and on translation failure, cancel teardown (parked + rendezvous + late-frame refusal), with the dead-query check correctly placed INSIDE run_fragment so the lease sweep at engine.rs:462-478 still runs. Extracting ParkedRegistry<F> into a non-gated module makes the park/claim/release/retire bookkeeping CI-testable for the first time (engine.rs is never compiled in CI); RetiredQueries is an Arc<Mutex> marked by both the engine Err arm and SiriusEngine::retire_query, so already-queued Runs are refused in both dispatch modes. The theoretical QUERY_FINISHED-vs-post-eos drop_parked race is practically closed by FIFO ordering (DropParked is enqueued right after rpc_transmit returns at nixl_transport.rs:790, long before an FE round trip) and would only produce a spurious drain error on a finished query. The refactor of the relay/export/release path is mechanical but is what pushes it past a quick review. Acceptance greps ('skipping fragment of a retired query', no 'fragment run started' after 'fragment run failed', QueryBegin allocated within 1 MB of baseline) match the plan literally; the 4-CN arm with q16 as the deliberate failure is runnable with capture-cn.sh 4.

result.reasoning: Delivery-side judgement. All three designs rest on the same verified mechanisms (engine.rs:267-275/282-318/697-717 wipe and park; compute_node_service.rs:380-390 worker, :864-911 Err arm with fail_query at :896, :457-479 cancel stub, :1358-1362 translate-before-slots; result_store.rs query_failures consulted only in reserve :127; local_exchange.rs take_ready :248-313 as the only removal; FE per-instance cancels with query_id at BackendServiceClient.java:192-206 and QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH only after eos at DefaultCoordinator.java:1027-1034) and the same measured evidence (headroom.txt base@start; cluster.log 6050-6305 for q05, 16585-16610 for q16; cn1-cnlog.txt cancels=N; refute-oom5/notes.md stolen time). B4 established this fix is hygiene and order-independence, not a pass/fail flip, so the value ceiling is fixed and the deciding criteria are blast radius, PR size, and how fast the acceptance arm runs. The surgical design gets the whole measured 1-CN effect in ~110 code lines in three files with a provably unchanged path for the 15 passing queries (no cancel-path change for reasons 5/1, one HashMap::get per Run), can be implemented in half a day in the already-built fix-parked-bookkeeping worktree (engine + CN built 15:51 today, GPUs idle now), and its smoke arm (q05 q06 q16 q17 q21 q22) runs in ~7 minutes with existing tooling (capture-cn.sh, run-queries.sh, headroom.txt, cnlog_extract.py). It is the '80% for 20%' version and the answer to whether a smaller version suffices is yes. result.summary: Fail fast at the reservation gate in gpu_pipeline_executor::manager_loop: inside the existing "after downgrade, reservation still partial" branch (gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:262-272), abort the query when the task is a retry, the downgrade freed 0 bytes, and reservation->size() + get_available_memory() is below the bytes its last OOM proved it needs (live_allocated + requested, a new size_t recorded beside the existing retry floor in gpu_pipeline_task.hpp). MAX_RETRIES=100 and the 50 ms backoff are untouched; the cross-GPU contention, CUDA-launch and sink-deferral retry paths never satisfy the predicate. Full design with code excerpts: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/oom-failfast-surgical.md
result.mechanism: Two facts the engine already certifies make the abort safe. (A) memory_space::make_reservation (cucascade/src/memory/memory_space.cpp:257-266) returns a partial grant only after notification_channel::wait() reports IDLE, which requires _n_active_notifiers == 0 (notification_channel.cpp:49-60); every reservation owns a notifier for its lifetime (reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:365-381, memory_reservation.hpp:183-198), so a partial grant means no in-flight reservation can free memory, and the grant is min(request, limit - allocated) (do_reserve_upto :535-543). (B) request_downgrade(...).get() returns bytes freed after sweeping TIER 1 repositories and TIER 2 queued tasks (downgrade_executor.cpp:223-300, :388-397); freed == 0 means nothing visible is convertible (parked sink output escapes the managers, streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112). (C) The OOM handlers already compute live_allocated + requested (gpu_pipeline_task.cpp:433-491 and :638-661) and fold it into update_retry_reservation_floor_after_oom (gpu_pipeline_task.hpp:99-108); the change records that sum as _oom_required_bytes, inherits it across reschedules (:110-114, executor :389), and the gate compares grant + available against it for retry_count > 0 && freed == 0. On a hit it logs, calls completion_handler->report_error(runtime_error(msg)) and breaks out of the manager loop exactly like the four existing gate failure paths (:195, :238, :260, :295); task_scheduler::drain_after_error restarts the loop (task_scheduler.cpp:265-311 -> task_executor.cpp:96-128). The message names bytes needed vs grantable, bytes held outside any live reservation vs pool, downgrade freed 0, retry number. It reaches the client unchanged through sirius_engine::execute (sirius_engine.cpp:263-278) -> streaming_fragment::run (:204-227) -> ffi::Fragment::run (sirius_ffi.cpp:990-1027) -> cxx::Exception (rust/crates/sirius/src/lib.rs:356) -> engine.rs:693-695 "failed to execute fragment" -> run_ready_fragment results.fail_query (compute_node_service.rs:864-910) -> fetch_data INTERNAL_ERROR (:523-528) -> FE ERROR 1064, the chain measured in cn1/runs/q05.r0.err. Measured basis: 17,917/17,917 gate passes in the six failure windows freed 0 and were partial (grant 3.08-3.32 GB vs floor up to 6.64 GB, q05), every OOM at global usage == 107374182400, no rescheduled task ever succeeded (retry_stats.py), 0 reschedule/partial lines outside the six windows on 1 CN and 0 on all cn4 CNs in the 4-CN window.

Every fuse/decline decision is taken with both sender and receiver params in hand before anything is deferred, and a decline falls back to today's run-and-park, so a wrong guess never changes results. Gap: no common_slot_map check on a leaf PROJECT root (would fail loudly via refuse_carried_join_child node_translator.rs:1880-1895, never silently). Predicts all six (q21 medium). Fusing F03 into F07 changes q21's odds in its favour: DuckDB then compares its join estimate for l1 x orders-F (~3e8 without column stats) against l3's 1.2e9 and keeps l3 as probe, whereas the surgical's exact 1.85e9 declared stream flips it. Mechanism verified: TPlan preorder splice is valid (PlanNodeCursor node_translator.rs:187-225, EXCHANGE num_children 0 at fragment-0137.txt:2541/3003), row_tuples guarantee holds (ExchangeNode.java:181-184; sender node 8 rt [6] fragment-0141.txt:11-18 vs exchange 9 irt [6] fragment-0137.txt:3020-3022), scan ranges keyed by query-global node id (scan_paths.rs:62-93), LocalPlan{params, inputs} carried recursively through execute_ready_fragment needs no alias map. A legitimate FE shape that passes today (a data-stream sender with output_exprs or a common-expr project) would fail under fusion. No such shape exists in the 22 TPC-H dumps (all six leaves out_exprs=None, sink output_columns None at fragment-0137.txt:3661/0140:1088/0141:821), and the fix is cheap (the sender params are in hand at defer time), but it must be fixed before implementation. result.winner: surgical (fragment-fusion-surgical.md) as the base, restructured with upstream's translator-module shape and refusal enum
result.reasoning: All three designs rest on the same verified mechanism and none is disqualified: replace a receiver's EXCHANGE_NODE (preorder leaf, num_children 0) by the single local sender's TPlan node list, union per_node_scan_ranges/node_to_per_driver_seq_scan_ranges (the leaves carry ranges in per_node_scan_ranges, fragment-0141.txt:4775, with node_to_per_driver Some({}) at :23178; ScanFilePaths::from_fragment reads both, scan_paths.rs:62-93), drop the exchange from per_exch_num_senders, and let the engine's DuckDB optimizer (sirius_ffi.cpp:134-138; JOIN_ORDER and BUILD_SIDE_PROBE_SIDE not in the disabled set :233-243) pick the build side. I re-checked every file:line the three designs cite in compute_node_service.rs (process_fragment 918-951, try_dispatch_sender 309-329, execute_fragment_with_inputs 1020-1246 incl. the one-destination gather rule 1104-1111 and sink checks 1079-1094, route_destination 1251-1275, execute_ready_fragment 1325-1394, receiver_exchanges 1397-1431, cancel_plan_fragment 457-479 result-store only, run_ready_fragment 864-911, translate_batch_attachment 1624-1679), local_exchange.rs (SenderSource 26-63, register_receiver 105-139, push_sender 142-155, push_remote_frame 159-246, take_ready 248-313), node_translator.rs (cursor 164-225, apply_fetch 258-297, translate_scan 341-356, translate_plan/merge_exchange_overrides/common_slots_consumed_above 390-560, translate_exchange 637-763, translate_hash_join 1722-1862 with no RIGHT_SEMI arm, refuse_carried_join_child 1880-1895, confine_carried 2338-2345, apply_conjuncts 2461-2493), lib.rs 247-437, agg_phase.rs 44-80, engine.rs (278-283 single request loop, 291-316 process-wide wipe, 486-729 declare/build/relay/run/park), FE (ExchangeNode.java 181-184 computeTupleIds; AllAtOnceExecutionSchedule.java:132 iterates getFragmentsInTopologicalOrderFromRoot, Deployer.java 208-215 waits per stage, so receiver-first is the default; enable_single_node_schedule defaults false at SessionVariable.java:3337), duckdb (TryFlipJoinChildren 160-213, SEMI/ANTI arm 225-244, GetBuildSize row-width metric 95-130), and the evidence (q04 HASH_JOIN id=6 type RIGHT_SEMI at cn1/engine-cn0.log:48480-48481; q05 RPC order at cluster.log:4142-4150; per_exch {7:1,9:1,13:1} at fragment-0137.txt:7703-7707). All check out. Two facts the designs assume that I confirmed from source: each of the six leaf senders carries exactly one conjunct (is_not_null_pred) so DuckDB estimates footer rows x 0.2 once, not per conjunct (relation_manager.cpp applies DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY once when datasource_filters is non-empty); and the translator never reads distribution_mode or partition_type (grep empty), so the FE's PARTITIONED label really is irrelevant to the engine. One measured claim in the surgical design's tooling is a false positive: parse_dumps.py reports out_cols=Some for middle fragments, but that regex matched TPlanNode.output_columns; the sink-level field is None (fragment-0137.txt:3661, 0140:1088), so all three designs' identity/None check is satisfied by every TPC-H fragment. Does each fix the measured case? Surgical: five of six, with q09 marginal (it keeps UNPARTITIONED broadcasts parked) and q21 most likely still failing; its own arithmetic for q21 is right because the exact declared cardinality of stream 9 (1.85e9) makes DuckDB build on the l3 scan estimated at 1.2e9 (actual 3.8e9). Upstream and robust: all six predicted, q21 medium, and fusing F03 too actually helps q21 (the join estimate ~3e8 vs l3 1.2e9 keeps l3 as probe). What can break for the 15 passing queries: surgical changes only q02/q07/q13/q20 (I re-derived this from survey/plan-summary.txt: the other 11 have only broadcast, gather or merge-fed shuffles), all four with build sides at least 5x apart; upstream and robust 'all' change about 13 of 15 and let DuckDB re-plan whole join trees with footer counts x 0.2 instead of exact stream counts, the BJ-4 hazard (q10 built on the 25.5 GB side). A wrong side is a memory/time regression (OOM bounded by fix 1), never a wrong answer, because a single-destination sink is the identity on rows and the exchange decorations that could change results (sort_info, limit, offset, conjuncts, merge-fed partial states) are either refused (surgical, upstream) or re-applied (robust). Cancellation: today cancel_plan_fragment is result-store only and LocalExchange only removes state in take_ready, so every design adds thrift-only host state that outlives a cancelled query; fusion strictly reduces GPU exposure (a deferred sender parks nothing) and robust alone ships forget_query; the others defer to fix 2. Acceptance soundness: upstream's is the best (fragment-run counts, off-switch reproduces the failure, 4-CN unchanged, oracle expectation split so the pre-existing 1e-3 decimal lowering on q05/q08/q09 revenue sums is not misread as a fusion bug; standalone matched exactly, compare-standalone-failed.txt, but the CN path does not for sums, compare-cn1.txt); surgical and robust both write 'oracle MATCH' for the six and would need that caveat. The one real as-written flaw is upstream's fold-time sender-side refusal turning a legitimate non-fusable shape into a query failure; surgical and robust decide before deferring. Weighing correctness and risk first: surgical wins (22) because it is a strict subset of upstream's behaviour, keeps 11 plans identical, keeps exact cardinalities at every non-leaf boundary, and needs no translator or remote-path change; upstream (19) is the right structure to grow into and has the best test plan; robust (15) buys the most coverage at the highest review and correctness surface and its 'all' default is the wrong first move. result.reasoning:
Method: read the plan, findings 3B/3C/4 and the three designs in full, then re-opened every cited file in /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf and re-counted the storm in scratchpad/perf/sf1000/cn1/engine-cn0.log.

Measured facts all three rest on, confirmed: 17,917 OOM lines (gpu_pipeline_task.cpp:458), every one GPU_SCAN index 0 with global usage 107374182400 and 0 bytes to materialize; 17,917 partial-after-downgrade lines, all '0 bytes freed'; 17,900 reschedules and 6 'exceeded' lines, none outside the six failure windows (retry_stats.py, cn1-cnlog.txt oom_resched=0 for the 15 passing queries). First retry-1 OOM per query: q05 +2.66 s, q08 +4.16, q09 +4.74, q17 +2.50, q18 +10.01, q21 +3.90 (round-1 lengths 1.05/2.43/2.36/1.30/0.72/1.22 s). Drain after report_error is 71 ms (engine-cn0.log:61723-61735), CN 'fragment run failed' 74 ms later (cluster.log:6049-6052).

Mechanisms confirmed: partial grants happen only when the notification channel is IDLE, i.e. no reservation alive on the space (memory_space.cpp:257-267, notification_channel.cpp:49-60, arena owns the notifier memory_reservation.hpp:183-198, raa.cpp:365-381); an upto grant is limit-allocated (raa.cpp:535-543, atomics.hpp:87-97); request_downgrade returns bytes freed after TIER 1 (repositories, downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232) and TIER 2 (queued tasks, :294-300); parked sink output escapes TIER 1 by design (streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112). The OOM handlers already compute live+requested and fold it into the floor (gpu_pipeline_task.cpp:433-492, :638-664, gpu_pipeline_task.hpp:99-114), fed back via :855/:886. The error string travels verbatim to the client; no CN/FE change needed for any design. The gate 'break' exits are recovered by drain_and_wait, which joins and restarts the manager (task_executor.cpp:96-128), so surgical's exit shape is valid.

Does each fix the measured case? Upstream: yes, with a wide margin (grant 3.08 GB < floor 6.64 GB, freed 0, at most one completion) and confirmed by the retry's own OOM; time-to-fail equals the first retry-1 OOM, one round later at worst. Surgical: yes if peak-live < requested at the failing allocation; the design's accounting argument (grant <= limit - P_oom ~ arena + overflow) gives grant < live+requested only under that unlogged condition, otherwise it is silently dormant -- flagged in its own open question with a one-line fallback. Robust: yes, but N=2 adds one round; with 2.4 s rounds q08/q09 land at ~6.6/7.1 s, above the plan's 5 s bar and unlike its predicted 3.8/4.5 s.

What can break for the 15 passing queries: nothing measurable in any design -- the changed branch is entered only on partial-after-downgrade with retry_count>0, which occurred 0 times in their windows on cn1 and all cn4 CNs. Robust adds three atomics and one has_error() load per task; upstream fills five integers per gate pass; surgical adds one dynamic_cast inside the partial branch. No data path changes, so oracle results cannot move. Cancellation: there is no engine-side cancel (compute_node_service.rs:449-476 is a stub); all three use first-error-wins report_error and the existing drain, so nothing new can wedge; robust is the only one that documents this.

Correctness differentiators: surgical aborts pre-emptively without a confirming OOM and without any progress signal; its IDLE + freed==0 argument is sound at the instant of the gate but blind to memory that becomes convertible afterwards (multi-GPU: GPU-resident batches skipped by the sweep while subscribed by the other GPU, downgrade_executor.cpp:231-232), which is the neighbourhood of the #732 contention case that motivated MAX_RETRIES=100. Upstream confirms by OOM and checks progress, but per executor (_tasks_executed, gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:310), so it shares a narrower version of the same multi-GPU blind spot. Robust's shared epoch plus in-flight first-attempt counter covers it, at the cost of the largest surface (config schema, ctor signatures at 3+9 sites, exception type at three throw sites, a counter whose leak silently changes behaviour) and some citation drift plus a wrong claim about HOST-tier executors (task_scheduler.cpp:91-93).

Acceptance soundness: all three correctly note the plan's '<= 5 s each' is unreachable for q18 (first OOM at +9.3 s). Surgical's '<= 1.5 s after first OOM' contradicts the measured 2.4 s round-1 for q08/q09; robust's numbers assume 1 s rounds; upstream's per-query table is the only one consistent with the measured rounds. Upstream's GPU-free predicate table is the most reviewer-friendly test; surgical's holder-task case is the best pin on the cucascade IDLE dependency and should be adopted.

Verdict: upstream wins (23 vs 20 vs 16) as the smallest change that fixes the measured case with a confirming OOM and a progress check, keeps the existing constants and hooks, and has the soundest acceptance plan; harden it with robust's scheduler-wide progress signals and metrics (without the config/ctor churn) and surgical's IDLE-pinning test and log assertions, and restate the fix-1 acceptance row relative to the first OOM with the measured round lengths.

result.title: fix(cn): retire a failed query's parked output instead of wiping every query's
result.summary: Base is the upstream design (judge 1's winner; judge 2's "surgical plus two mandatory upstream merges" converges on the same core). Parked sender output on the CN becomes query-scoped: a new CI-compiled `parked_registry.rs` (`ParkedRegistry<F>` + bounded `RetiredQueries`) replaces the three loose maps in engine.rs, the process-wide wipe at engine.rs:291-316 becomes a per-query `retire`, and a shared `Arc<Mutex<RetiredQueries>>` marked on the engine thread (or by `SiriusEngine::retire_query` before a fire-and-forget `RetireQuery` request) refuses already-queued runs in both dispatch modes. Four gates: refusal as the first statement inside `run_fragment_inner` so the remote-input lease sweep at engine.rs:462-478 still runs; a park-time refusal for output finished after its query was retired; a dispatch-worker gate at the top of `run_ready_fragment` that releases staged batches and emits no `fragment run started`; an arrival gate in `process_fragment` that keeps the result-fragment reserve-then-fail contract. `fail_fragment` (fail_query + retire_query) covers the q16 translation case, and a `StagedLeases` drop guard releases arena leases on every pre-run error path. Commit 2 makes `cancel_plan_fragment` a real teardown (every reason retires parked + rendezvous state via `LocalExchange::retire_receiver`/`is_retired` with a HashSet twin; only failure reasons record `cancel_query`), refuses late remote frames, and records inline-path failures at query level. Merged from robust: `AlreadyTornDown` idempotent release, structured retire log fields, the `skipping fragment of a retired query` grep target. Merged from surgical: RetiredQueries capacity 1024, the unlabelled-failure GPU test, the cancel-reason matrix test, the acceptance arithmetic. Not merged: TTL sweep, knobs, Inventory, fail_query_all, three-PR split. One correction to upstream's split: the RetireQuery request belongs in commit 1 because fail_fragment needs it. No engine C++, FE, proto or knob changes; two commits, ~550 non-test + ~800 test lines, ~2 engineer-days + one GPU session.

result.title: fix(pipeline): fail the query fast when an OOM retry cannot make progress
result.summary: The two judges tied (surgical 43, upstream 43, robust 32) and asked for the same merges, so the spec is that merge: the decision is made in the executor's reschedule path (upstream's shape, confirmed by the retry's own OOM, same exit as the MAX_RETRIES path) using surgical's hard lower bound `live + requested` recorded by the OOM handler (replacing upstream's `granted < floor` test, which judge 2 showed is always true because the floor is raised to >= 2x granted before the throw), a pure header-only predicate with a GPU-free Catch2 table, and robust's scheduler-wide progress signals (`completed_epoch` + `inflight_first_attempts` in a small struct owned by task_scheduler, passed through a defaulted extra ctor argument so the one test construction site keeps compiling) plus its `has_error()` early-out at the gate and `oom_reschedules`/`futile_aborts` metrics. Rule: OOM exception, retry_count >= 1, gate granted less than requested (partial grant, which cucascade issues only when no other reservation is alive: memory_space.cpp:257-266, notification_channel.cpp:49-60), downgrade freed 0, OOM-recorded need > grant, epoch unchanged since the gate, no first attempt in flight anywhere. MAX_RETRIES=100 and the 50 ms backoff are untouched (hoisted to file scope); no config, CN, FE, proto or cucascade change; the error text travels verbatim to the client through the verified existing path and names bytes needed vs grantable, bytes held outside any task reservation vs the pool (exact under IDLE: limit - grant), bytes freed, disk-tier state. Predicted SF1000 effect (inference from the measured chain, re-run of retry_stats.py today): each of q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 fails one retry round after its first OOM (client ~2.9/4.3/4.9/2.6/10.2/4.0 s vs 101.5/168.3/232.5/103.9/54.2/114.5 s today); the 15 passing queries never enter the changed branch (0 reschedule lines in their windows on cn1 and cn4). Touched engine files are byte-identical between origin/dev and the perf base (only task_scheduler.{hpp,cpp} differ by +53 non-overlapping lines), so the PR can target dev self-contained.

result.build_order_notes: Land fix 1 first: engine-only, no shared files with fix 2 (Rust), fix 3 (FE patch) or fix 4 (CN/translator, streaming_fragment.cpp, downgrade_executor.cpp, sirius_ffi.cpp), and it shortens every later SF1000 arm by ~12 minutes. Interactions: fix 2 moves the CN's Err arm from +100 s to +3 s and removes the leftover-fragment time (q17 -> q18 6.42 s) that lands in arm A's runs.csv numbers, which is why the primary criterion is measured from the first OOM in the engine log; fix 2's tests must not assume the failure arrives after other senders have parked. Fix 4b (spillable parked repositories) makes freed > 0 at these gates so the rule stays quiet while spilling progresses and fires only once HOST is full and nothing completes (intended division of labour); fix 4a (fusion) removes the OOM for the six and this stays the safety net. Fix 3 orthogonal. Measurement branch stays on perf/profile-sf1000 (45dab3be) in the fix-oom-failfast worktree; the PR is a cherry-pick onto a fork branch off origin/dev (touched engine files identical; only task_scheduler.{hpp,cpp} differ by +53 non-overlapping lines, so re-check `git diff origin/dev..d24f02c4 -- src/pipeline/task_scheduler.cpp src/include/pipeline/task_scheduler.hpp` when placing the three-line edits). **Verdict.** The four specs are compatible; no redesign needed. Landing order: **fix 1 (engine) -> fix 2 (CN bookkeeping) -> fix 4a (fusion, rebased on fix 2) -> plan item 5 (RIGHT_SEMI translator arm) -> fix 3 (FE patch + proto)**. Fix 1 shares no files; fix 2 owns the cancel/removal path fusion needs; fix 3 goes last because its FE rebuild is the long pole, its EXPLAIN gate must precede any 1-CN sweep, and its plan changes invalidate fusion's golden counts.

**Interactions found (all verified against source at 45dab3be):**
- Fix 1 vs fix 2: same Err path, just ~100 s earlier and with a new text. The dispatch worker is a single FIFO thread (`compute_node_service.rs:380-391`), so which senders had parked before the failure is decided by queue order, not time; fix 2's `slots=2` acceptance holds. Landing-order contradiction (fix 1 "land first" vs fix 2 "before fix 1's arm") resolved: code order 1 then 2, arms as in the matrix.
- Fix 1 vs fix 4a: **wrong prediction fixed**. A fused q21's join build lives in inter-pipeline repositories (`repository_wiring_materializer.cpp:68-69`) that TIER 1 spills to HOST, so `freed > 0` and fix 1's rule 5 keeps retrying; "with fix 1 it dies in seconds" does not hold for fused shapes.
- Fix 2 vs fix 4a: both edit `cancel_plan_fragment`, `execute_ready_fragment`, `process_fragment`, `local_exchange.rs`, `DEMO.md:37-42`. Resolution: fix 2 owns cancellation (`retire_receiver` already removes a deferred `LocalPlan`; fusion's `forget_query` dropped); fold before fix 2's input split; and a gap closed: on the async path `exec_single_attachment` (`:705-717`) calls `try_dispatch_sender` before `process_fragment`, so fusion's hook runs before fix 2's gate 4 -> fusion's `try_defer_sender` now checks `failure_of` first.
- Fix 3 vs fix 4a: complementary. Fix 3's predicted q03/q12 BROADCAST->PARTITIONED flips at 1 CN (78/36 GB parked) are exactly the leaf shape `leaf` fuses, so fix 4a must be in any knob-on 1-CN build. `TUNABLES.md` insertion point collides (both after "Engine-side").
- Fix 3 vs fixes 1/2: orthogonal; translate-only survey unaffected by gate 4 / fusion hook.
